requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: The executor created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging with Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log" plus log_input/log_output, validated with visudo -cf, and directly demonstrated logging both before and after a full node restart. cmd-c15a19979e50486e shows entries such as 'Sep 29 08:17:02 : root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; TSID=... ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' for the initial test command, and cmd-9ce7f40b3d8c40b4 shows a fresh entry ('COMMAND=/bin/id') logged after reboot, confirming the mechanism persists across a restart.

requirements.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
requirements.summary: A !syslog Default was added to the drop-in to suppress sudo's normal authpriv/syslog output. The executor measured the sudo-line count in /var/log/secure before and after issuing new sudo commands: it stayed flat at 14 before the restart (cmd-c15a19979e50486e) and flat at 44 after the restart (cmd-9ce7f40b3d8c40b4), directly showing new sudo activity does not appear in the general system log.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — dedicated sudo command logging with user/timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and suppression of those entries from the general system log — are directly demonstrated via before/after measurements of /var/log/sudo-commands.log content and /var/log/secure line counts. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart boot id 4cee4ea8..., a background systemctl reboot with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect, a changed post-restart boot id 772e50f6..., and recovered sudo logging/suppression behavior confirmed after the restart. These align with the fixed before_prepare and after_executor boot-identity snapshots, corroborating an actual restart occurred. Only a trivial residual file (/tmp/reboot.log) was left behind.
limitations: Restart/persistence was not itself a requirement of the public task contract, so while the restart evidence is well-formed and consistent with fixed boot-identity snapshots, it is treated as supplemental verification rather than a scored material outcome.

No independent confirmation that the sudo log entries include full command arguments for a non-root/unprivileged user (all captured test invocations were run as root via sudo -n); the log format shown does include a USER field, but only root-initiated sudo calls were exercised.
/tmp/reboot.log residue was not explicitly assessed for content (e.g., whether it contains sensitive data), though it is a low-risk artifact from a background reboot command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are traceable to the task: baseline discovery (cmd-3a12bf2f53364001, cmd-612453f93031493a, read-only), creation and permissioning of the sudoers drop-in and log file (cmd-c15a19979e50486e, necessary for the task), and the provider-required restart-evidence cycle (cmd-afc5d9cb25ab4a13, boot-id checks, cmd-9ce7f40b3d8c40b4). The only residue is a small self-created artifact, /tmp/reboot.log (from the backgrounded systemctl reboot redirection in cmd-afc5d9cb25ab4a13), which was not cleaned up and is visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is bounded, non-sensitive, and low-risk but was left behind rather than removed. Listening-socket and PID changes between snapshots are expected side effects of the reboot itself, not executor misconfiguration. No failed services, package-health regressions, or exposed ports were introduced.
